title: The Transfer Order
subtitle: A popular teacher is transferred overnight after a complaint; parents block the school gate
coldOpen: 07:30. A transfer order moves a teacher 200 km today.
08:00. Parents lock the school gate from inside.
The complaint behind the order is sealed.

briefing.grievance: Parents say the teacher who turned the school around is being removed on an anonymous complaint, with no hearing. The education office says the complaint is serious and sealed. Children are inside.
knownFacts: The transfer order cites “administrative grounds” and gives one day’s notice.
A complaint was filed four days ago; its contents are sealed.
Four hundred children are inside the locked school.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the complaint alleges abuse of a child.
Parents say the complaint came from a contractor the teacher refused to pay.
briefing.responsibility: You run the district education office. The order is yours to pause, confirm or explain.
briefing.objective: Give the teacher a fair process, protect the complainant and the children, and get the gate open without a fight.

rightsMoments.question: A teacher is transferred overnight on a sealed complaint with no hearing. What does natural justice require?

options.text: Notice of the allegation, a chance to answer, an impartial decision-maker and reasons in writing before any adverse action.
options.feedback: Correct. Adverse action on a complaint without a hearing violates natural justice, however urgent the pressure.

options.text: Nothing; transfers are administrative and need no reasons.
options.feedback: A transfer used as punishment on a complaint is adverse action and attracts the right to be heard.

options.text: Clear the teacher publicly to end the protest.
options.feedback: Pre-judging in either direction denies the complainant and the teacher a fair process.

rightsMoments.principle: Natural justice (audi alteram partem, Article 14) requires notice, a hearing and reasons before adverse action, and protection for complainants against reprisal.
rightsMoments.why: A hearing with the accounts on the table found the facts; a quiet transfer would have punished the one who noticed.

simple.question: A teacher is moved overnight on a secret complaint with no hearing. What is fair?

options.a: Tell him the charge, let him answer, decide fairly, give reasons in writing.
options.c: Declare him innocent to end the protest.

feedback.a: Yes! Hear both sides before acting against anyone.
feedback.b: No. A transfer used as punishment needs a hearing.
feedback.c: Deciding before the hearing is unfair to both sides.

simple.principle: Hear both sides before acting against anyone. Give reasons in writing. Protect the complainant too.
simple.why: A hearing with the accounts found the facts. A quiet transfer would have punished the one who noticed.
